name: The Bahamas

income_tax.summary: There is no personal income tax in The Bahamas. National Insurance is 4.65% of wages for employees and 10.3% for the self-employed, up to a weekly ceiling of BSD 830 (BSD 43,160 a year).
income_tax.self_employed_notes: Self-employed pay 10.3% of average insurable income to the National Insurance Board (NIB). Self-employed people trading locally may also owe the turnover-based annual business licence fee (Deloitte); not modelled. Cap shown is the PwC weekly ceiling BSD 830 x 52.
income_tax.local_tax_note: No income tax, no local income surtax. No health levy appears on the PwC or Deloitte pages.

sources.title: PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries: The Bahamas, Individual - Taxes on personal income
PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries: The Bahamas, Individual - Other taxes

open_questions: NIB wage ceiling: PwC (reviewed 21 July 2026) gives BSD 830 a week and the 10.3% self-employed rate; Deloitte's January 2026 highlights give BSD 3,510 a month / BSD 810 a week, 'last adjusted July 2024'. PwC's newer figure is used; the NIB site is a script-only page and could not be read.

regimes.name: Bahamas Extended Access Travel Stay (BEATS)
regimes.description: Annual residence permit for professionals working remotely for a non-Bahamian employer or on their own account, and for students studying remotely. The Bahamas has no personal income tax, so the permit changes access, not tax.
regimes.duration_note: Permit valid 12 months; annual renewals are considered for a maximum of three years. Fee USD 25 application + USD 1,000 permit for an individual; family adds USD 25 + USD 500 per dependant (renewal fees not listed).

sources.title: Bahamas Extended Access Travel Stay (BEATS): FAQ

open_questions: No minimum income is published on the official FAQ (job letter or proof of self-employment only); some third-party guides quote a threshold, not verified.
The official pages do not address tax or National Insurance for BEATS holders.
The 'professionals' page is the official FAQ; the 3-year maximum is the FAQ's wording ('considered for a maximum of three years').

costs.notes: No reliable long-term 1-bed or 2-bed rent was found. Coldwell Banker Bahamas lists only luxury homes (USD 15,000 to 55,000); Bahamas Realty returned HTTP 403; the Bahamas Real Estate Association site lists vacation rentals only; Numbeo returned HTTP 429 on two attempts and Expatistan HTTP 403.

residence_routes: Remote workers of any citizenship (EU, US, other) can use BEATS: a 12-month permit renewable annually for up to three years, USD 1,025 for an individual. Employees of a Bahamian employer need a work permit (not researched). Permanent residence is by economic investment of BSD 1 million or more (Department of Immigration, per repo research in data/jurisdictions/BHS.json); that route is not tied to income. US citizens remain taxable in the US on worldwide income; the Bahamas has no tax to credit.
open_questions: No rent data; Nassau long-term 1-bed/2-bed rents need a listing source that can be opened (several agent sites block automated access).
